subject: Clarification on UK Addendum, TIA scope, and routing via third-country CDN
messages:
From: Emma Sutton <emma.sutton@medicitech.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: dpo@medicitech.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Data routing & UK Addendum questions for upcoming engagement

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the recent call — quick follow-up from our legal/dev teams. Two specific questions before we proceed with the pilot:

1) Our architecture uses a third-party CDN (edge nodes in India) that may temporarily cache request metadata. Under the UK Addendum / IDTA, do you consider transient CDN caching as an international transfer requiring TIA coverage, or can this be covered by subprocessor attestations?

2) We need a minimal evidence package for procurement: current subprocessor list with regions, whether Redwood provides a UK Addendum + TIA (if routing touches non-EEA/UK nodes), and a suggested fallback routing policy if a CDN edge is in-scope.

Can you share a short timeline for evidence and whether Redwood can commit to EU/UK-only egress for the pilot if required?

Appreciate a response within 48 hours if possible — procurement needs to triage.

Best,
Emma Sutton
Legal Counsel | Medici Technologies
[attachment: medicitech_scope.pdf]

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Emma Sutton <emma.sutton@medicitech.com>
Cc: dpo@medicitech.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 11:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data routing & UK Addendum questions for upcoming engagement

Emma — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (legal/compliance) and Marissa (privacy ops) so we can pull the right artifacts.

High level: Redwood treats transient CDN caching as processing by a subprocessor in the country where caching occurs. That means it can be in-scope for transfer safeguards. We commonly address this two ways:

- Provide subprocessor attestations + documented mitigations (TTL, no persisted payloads) when the CDN is limited to metadata caching; or
- Include CDN within the TIA/DTIA scope and offer routing fallback to EU/UK-only egress for sensitive workloads.

I will confirm which evidence set we can share for the pilot (subprocessor map + draft TIA scope) and whether we can enforce EU/UK egress for your pilot tenancy. Expect an internal update in ~3–6 business hours and full package within 48 hours.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 13:25:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data routing & UK Addendum questions for upcoming engagement

Priya / Marissa — quick triage notes:

- Subprocessor map: latest canonical (v2) lives in GDrive; contains region columns and subprocessors that perform caching (CDN partners). I will export a redacted PDF for procurement.
- TIA approach: for CDNs that only cache ephemeral metadata we can provide attestations stating no persistent storage of customer payloads and short TTLs; legal prefers to include an explicit TIA when routing could hit India nodes to avoid ambiguity.
- Fallback: product can pin egress region per-tenant and we can lock pilot to eu-west-1 / eu-west-2. Need a config ticket to ops (I will raise).

Marissa — can you assemble: (a) redacted subprocessor_map_v2.pdf, (b) draft TIA scope document that includes explicit CDN treatment and fallback routing language, and (c) short mitigation description for ephemeral caching? Goal: send consolidated package to Emma.

K

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 May 2026 09:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data routing & UK Addendum questions for upcoming engagement

Attached first pass of artifacts. See notes below.

Attachments:
- redwood_subprocessor_map_v2.pdf (redacted for public-facing procurement)
- redwood_tia_scope-draft.docx (draft; highlights CDN handling)

Notes (short):
- CDN handling: we mark CDN edge nodes as "transient processing" and require partners to accept a limited processing addendum that forbids payload persistence; copies of partner attestations are included where available.
- Evidence: we can supply the redacted map + partner attestations for the specific CDN on record. Full partner contracts require an NDA / legal review.
- Routing: Product can enforce EU/UK-only egress at tenant creation; however, CDN edge selection is ultimately client-selected unless we run the CDN as part of our managed stack. For the pilot we can set the tenancy to EU/UK-only and add an operational SLO to ensure egress restrictions.

I'll prepare a short cover note for procurement (1 page) and the attachments you can send to Medici.

-Marissa
Privacy Ops | Redwood Inference

From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 22 May 2026 08:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Data routing & UK Addendum questions for upcoming engagement

Emma — thanks for flagging. Quick consolidated answers and next steps below.

Summary answers:
- Transient CDN caching: considered subprocessor processing in the country where the edge node resides. If caching is strictly ephemeral (short TTL, no payload persistence) we can provide partner attestations. If you prefer legal certainty, we are prepared to include the CDN within the TIA/DTIA scope.
- Evidence package: attached redwood_subprocessor_map_v2.pdf (redacted) and redwood_tia_scope-draft.docx. The draft TIA explicitly calls out CDN behavior and fallback routing language.
- EU/UK-only egress: we can lock your pilot tenancy to EU/UK egress (eu-west-1 and eu-west-2) and add an operational SLO that blocks outbound routing to non-EU/UK egress for the pilot. This will prevent requests from being proxied through third-country nodes under our managed tenancy.

Requested actions / next steps:
1) Please confirm if Medici prefers (A) partner attestations + mitigations for CDN edges, or (B) CDN included in the TIA scope (we recommend B for high-sensitivity workloads).
2) Sign a short, mutual NDA if you want full partner contracts or unredacted evidence. We can start the EU/UK-only tenancy config as soon as you confirm.
3) If you accept the draft TIA language, legal can route comments to kimberly_park@redwood.com; procurement can reference the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cRedwoodSubprocessors

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessor_map_v2.pdf, redwood_tia_scope-draft.docx

Happy to run a 30m sync with your security/team if helpful — available Mon/Tue next week.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
